neighbours.label: a sudden turn or surprise in a narrative (face fell, only to find, soon found out, WOW)
fire: Maria grinned as she read the letter, until her expression suddenly fell.
We raced to the station, only to discover the train had left.
He expected a quiet evening, but he soon realised the house was full of guests.
I tore off the wrapping and, WOW, it was the guitar I had wanted.
The children ran to the beach, only to see the tide was already in.
Tom laughed at the joke, then his smile vanished when he saw the bill.
She thought the exam would be easy, but she quickly learned otherwise.
Upon opening the fridge, he gasped: it was completely empty.
quiet: Maria smiled as she read the letter and then put it in a drawer.
We walked to the station and caught the train at noon.
He expected a quiet evening, and he spent it reading in the garden.
I took off the wrapping and put the guitar on the stand.
The children walked to the beach and built a sandcastle.
Tom laughed at the joke and asked the waiter for the bill.
She studied for the exam and passed it with a good mark.
He opened the fridge and took out some milk for his tea.

notes: Probe: 'his face suddenly fell' 0.79, 'only to find' 0.80, 'soon found out' 0.70, 'WOW' 0.54, plain 'walked in' 0.16.
